These findings emphasize the necessity for dermatologists to enhance patient monitoring and education throughout the treatment process. Our results demonstrated that the median time to onset of tralokinumab-related AEs was 37 days, with most occurring within the first month of treatment. Only 14% of AEs occurred after 6 months of treatment, a clinically significant finding. This result suggests that the risk of tralokinumab-related AEs decreases significantly after six months of treatment, and clinicians may consider adjusting monitoring strategies accordingly. Timely identification of AEs by healthcare professionals is crucial for rapidly implementing preventive strategies and minimizing clinical impact on patients. However, no difference in the timing of conjunctivitis onset was observed between tralokinumab and dupilumab in this study; enhanced monitoring for specific AEs (e.g., conjunctivitis and keratitis) remains necessary in patients with AD treated with biologic agents to mitigate the impact of serious AEs. Conclusion This study conducted a comprehensive pharmacovigilance analysis of tralokinumab-associated AEs using FAERS data, identifying potential safety signals not listed on the product label: eczema herpeticum, generalized exfoliative dermatitis, hair loss, skin exfoliation, and eyelid inflammation. Notably, eczema herpeticum, generalized exfoliative dermatitis, and skin exfoliation may reflect severe AD manifestations rather than true drug-related AEs, highlighting the risk of misclassifying disease vs. treatment-related events. Comparative analysis with dupilumab revealed differential AE profiles: dupilumab had higher injection-site reaction reporting rates, while tralokinumab showed higher conjunctivitis and keratitis rates. These findings inform post-market safety monitoring and clinical decision-making by highlighting underrecognized tralokinumab-associated AEs requiring closer monitoring. However, results should be interpreted cautiously due to limitations in the FAERS database (reporting biases and underreporting) and the observational study design. This study generates hypotheses that require validation through well-designed clinical trials to confirm safety signals, establish causal relationships, and characterize tralokinumab’s safety profile. Prospective trials with rigorous designs and larger sample sizes are needed to determine the accurate AE incidence rates, while mechanistic studies should elucidate underlying pathways and risk factors.

documents.title: BAD guidelines for the management of atopic eczema in children

chunks.content: Background Food allergy affects 8% of US children, with peanut allergy (PA) being the most prevalent (2.2%) [ ]. The Learning Early About Peanut (LEAP) study demonstrated that early introduction of peanuts to infants reduces the likelihood of developing PA in high-risk infants [ , ]. Therefore, the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) published the 2017 Addendum Guidelines for the Prevention of Peanut Allergy (PPA) [ ]. The guidelines stated that infants aged 4–6 months should be screened for PA risk and receive peanut introduction recommendations according to their risk level. Infants at high-risk (with severe eczema or egg allergy) should have a peanut specific Immunoglobulin E test conducted and/or should be referred to an allergist before peanut-containing foods are introduced. Infants at low-risk (with no or mild/moderate eczema) should begin eating peanut-containing foods at around 6 months of age or according to family preferences or cultural norms. By adhering to these guidelines, pediatric clinicians may contribute to reducing the incidence of PA. Despite the potential benefits of PPA guideline adherence, a 2018 national survey of pediatricians reported that only 1/3 of pediatricians used the guidelines fully as published [ ]. Limitations of this survey include that it was conducted 1.5 years after the guidelines were released and that pediatricians more familiar with the guidelines may have been more likely to respond. In contrast, electronic health records (EHRs) enable observation of real-world, documented practices via structured (e.g., prescriptions, diagnosis codes) and unstructured data (e.g., outpatient clinical notes and hospital discharge summaries). PPA guideline adherence (appropriate peanut introduction recommendations based on risk level) and PA risk factors are commonly documented within clinical notes in EHRs. However, while structured EHR data lends itself to data processing and analytics, the complexity of unstructured data poses a significant challenge because of the use of shorthand and variations in terminology and syntax. These challenges increase when studying data across practice sites and networks, with different note template formats and EHR interfaces. Manual labeling and extraction of information from an extensive volume of clinical text can be laborious, costly, and subject to human error. Therefore, clinical Natural Language Processing (NLP), a specialized application of NLP techniques to understand clinical notes, may be a valuable tool for analyzing and interpreting unstructured medical datasets from EHRs [ ]. NLP has proven to be useful in many healthcare applications [ – ] and is effective in identifying patients with food allergy based on well-child care (WCC) visit notes [ ]. In a pharmacovigilance study, one hour spent developing an NLP system reduced 20 hours of manual chart review; the time saved allowed the study team to focus their manual chart review on the 25% of the cohort that needed it [ ]. NLP can be used to compare free text data documented during standard clinical care across randomized controlled trial arms. For PA prevention, a multifaceted intervention was developed to support pediatric clinician adherence to the PPA guidelines. The Intervention to Reduce Early (Peanut) Allergy in Children (iREACH) trial included clinician education, an EHR integrated clinical decision support (CDS) tool in 4- and 6-month WCC visits, and follow-up EHR prompts in 9- and 12-month WCC visits. Clinicians in the control arm did not receive study-specific education or tools. A two-arm, cluster-randomized, controlled clinical trial was designed to evaluate the effectiveness of the intervention to increase pediatric clinician adherence to the PPA guidelines and decrease the incidence of PA. The pragmatic design of the iREACH trial meant that pediatric clinicians generated study data within the context of standard clinical practice, as recorded in the EHR. The iREACH trial design has previously been published [ ]. The purpose of this work is to describe the development of an NLP pipeline across three practice networks to identify peanut introduction recommendations and severe eczema. This work supports measurement of the iREACH trial’s primary outcome of pediatric clinician adherence to the PPA guidelines. Methods Study design The iREACH trial involved thirty pediatric practices from three practice networks in Illinois: Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children’s Pediatric Practice Research Group (PPRG), AllianceChicago (Alliance), and PPRG-Peoria. Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children’s Hospital’s Data Analytics and Reporting team served as the data coordinating center and was responsible for developing and implementing the NLP pipeline. The networks included federally qualified health centers (Alliance), as well as independent (PPRG), hospital-owned (PPRG), and health care system-owned practices (PPRG-Peoria). Practice sites were randomized into control ( n = 14) and intervention ( n = 16) groups. During 18-month periods from November 2020 to October 2022, pediatric clinicians’ EHR data were extracted from 4- and 6- month WCC visits, for measurement of the primary outcome. Patient data The study database, a central data repository for the iREACH trial (Fig. ), included structured patient data such as demographic variables,

center and was responsible for developing and implementing the NLP pipeline. The networks included federally qualified health centers (Alliance), as well as independent (PPRG), hospital-owned (PPRG), and health care system-owned practices (PPRG-Peoria). Practice sites were randomized into control ( n = 14) and intervention ( n = 16) groups. During 18-month periods from November 2020 to October 2022, pediatric clinicians’ EHR data were extracted from 4- and 6- month WCC visits, for measurement of the primary outcome. Patient data The study database, a central data repository for the iREACH trial (Fig. ), included structured patient data such as demographic variables, visit types, visit diagnoses, problem lists, and medications. A common data dictionary was established to ensure that extract, transform, and load (ETL) processes generated interoperable data with standardized variable names, formats, and permissible values across all data sources. Clinical notes were also collected. Clinical notes were almost exclusively in English; however, a small number of clinical notes contained Spanish text. Clinical notes from PPRG-Peoria and PPRG (both based on Epic ) were structurally different from those of Alliance (based on Centricity). Notes from PPRG-Peoria and PPRG had a combination of free and templated text in sections, with some discrete data elements, including those generated via the CDS, inserted as text. Conversely, notes from Alliance were compilations of named data elements that required a text synthesis step to create narrative style notes that were similar to those from the other networks. The NLP processing focused on clinical notes related to the 4- and 6- month WCC visits only. Clinical notes were associated with a “note type,” and the use of these labels varied across the networks. At PPRG, 96% of the clinical notes for these visits from the start of the trial (11/2020) through 11/2022 were labeled as progress notes or patient instructions. All other note types (e.g. addendum notes, assessment and plan notes, confidential notes, nursing notes, and telephone encounters) were excluded from the NLP processing. At Alliance, 88% of the clinical notes were labeled as “office notes.” At PPRG-Peoria, 81% of the clinical notes were labeled as progress notes or patient instructions. Since the study team had less experience with clinical notes from Alliance and PPRG-Peoria, all note types from these networks were included in the NLP processing. NLP pipeline An NLP pipeline was developed to process clinical notes using CLAMP (Melax Technologies, Inc., Houston, Texas), a comprehensive NLP software package that facilitates recognition and encoding of clinical information within textual data [ ]. Developers can construct a customized NLP pipeline by selectively choosing components that manage NLP tasks such as sentence detection, tokenization, part-of-speech tagging, text chunking, and biomedical named entity recognition. By implementing a set of rules, multiple annotations related to these named entities were enhanced to create more meaningful and easily identifiable concepts. This process involved enriching the initial annotations produced by the NLP system, making them more comprehensive and contextually relevant. For example, when the NLP system identified a term related to peanut introduction or severe eczema, the implemented rules allowed for more information to be added to the annotation, such as the context in which the term was used or its relationship to other medical conditions mentioned in the text. This augmentation helped in transforming raw data into structured, clinically meaningful concepts that were easily recognized and then were used in downstream analyses. Finally, association rules were applied to detect the presence of, negation of, or irrelevant reference to key concepts. NLP pre-processing The initial phase of the NLP pipeline involves pre-processing all clinical notes to ensure accurate processing. Clinical notes often contained special characters that can cause misinterpretation by the NLP system. To address this, unnecessary characters (such as double spacing, leftover XML tags, or XML strings) were eliminated, while the semantic integrity of the clinical notes was preserved. Algorithm development NLP peanut recommendation The study aimed to identify, during infants’ 4- or 6-month WCC visits, pediatric clinicians’ recommendations to introduce peanut-containing foods. The goal was to find any pertinent text that documented: (1) having discussed peanut introduction and/or (2) that peanut products were already in the infant’s diet; both scenarios were considered clinician adherence to the PPA guidelines. To achieve the goal, a named entity dictionary was established, encompassing all relevant peanut products. The peanut product had to be clearly defined, and not in general terms such as “food” or “allergenic foods.”]. The dictionary included: “peanut," "nut butters," "PB" (for peanut butter), and commercial products used for early peanut introduction, such as peanut powders and puffs. Peanut product concepts were then linked to a recommendation concept by creating another dictionary with keywords which included “recommend,” “introduce,” “expose,” “try,” and “discuss.” These two dictionaries were used to find the two concepts (“peanut product” and “recommendation”) together in a sentence. For example, “introduce peanut

a named entity dictionary was established, encompassing all relevant peanut products. The peanut product had to be clearly defined, and not in general terms such as “food” or “allergenic foods.”]. The dictionary included: “peanut," "nut butters," "PB" (for peanut butter), and commercial products used for early peanut introduction, such as peanut powders and puffs. Peanut product concepts were then linked to a recommendation concept by creating another dictionary with keywords which included “recommend,” “introduce,” “expose,” “try,” and “discuss.” These two dictionaries were used to find the two concepts (“peanut product” and “recommendation”) together in a sentence. For example, “introduce peanut products if low risk.” While having the two distinct concepts indicate a peanut recommendation was made, it was not always necessary or relevant to have both. To account for situations in which (1) templated patient instruction text included a solid, strongly implied peanut introduction recommendation, or (2) peanut products were already in the infant’s diet, exceptions were made to the aforementioned two-concept rule. Examples include this templated instruction wording -- “there is no evidence that further delaying the introduction of highly allergenic foods (such as eggs, nut products, fish, and shellfish) beyond 6 months old will have any impact on whether or not your child develops food allergies” -- and that peanut products already had been introduced -- “Interval History: rash on abdomen after spoonful one.” These exceptions allowed the study team to identify more recommendations. NLP severe eczema Identification of severe eczema (or “atopic dermatitis”) in the text notes was necessary to categorize the risk of PA and to apply the PPA guidelines to determine clinicians’ adherence. The study team and subject matter experts defined severe eczema and formulated a comprehensive algorithm. Our definition of severe eczema was informed by the NIAID guidelines but was adapted to reflect how eczema severity is documented in the EHR. First, keywords that were dispositive and that limited the text from further consideration were defined. For example, if a healthcare provider classified eczema as “severe,” no further analysis of the text was necessary. Similarly, if the provider classified the eczema as “moderate” or “mild,” the eczema in that note was not characterized as “severe.” In cases where eczema was not characterized as “severe,” “moderate,” or “mild,” the NLP analyzed the note for descriptions of the physical examination of the skin. The NLP looked for the following keywords (or variants thereof) as descriptions of the eczema: “crusting,” “scaly,” “thickening,” “lichenification,” “oozing,” and “scabbing”. Presence of any of these descriptions was categorized as severe eczema if the structured data in the iREACH trial database’s medication table included any severe eczema-relevant medication (Fig. ). The list of medications was defined by clinical experts from the research team. Certain topical medications (such as hydrocortisone ≥ 2.5%, other steroids like desonide and triamcinolone in any form or strength, or calcineurin inhibitors like tacrolimus) or related oral medications were indicative of severe eczema. Topical creams with 1% hydrocortisone (typically an over-the-counter medication) were not considered to be a medication indicative of severe eczema. Finally, exclusions were applied to seborrheic dermatitis (cradle cap), a common infant scalp condition consisting of patches with oily, yellow scales or crusts. Unlike eczema, seborrheic dermatitis is not a risk factor for PA. If seborrheic dermatitis and eczema were mentioned in the same sentence, descriptions of the eczema were evaluated separately from the seborrheic dermatitis. NLP iterative development process The NLP algorithms for peanut recommendation and severe eczema underwent multiple iterations during development to enhance their performance. The development of the NLP was organized into three main phases: exploratory, training, and validation (Fig. ). In the training phase, the remaining two networks (Alliance and PPRG-Peoria) were also included. Random samples of 400 patients from PPRG and 100 each from Alliance and PPRG-Peoria who had 4- or 6-month WCC visits from 2020 to 2022 were used for the training sets. The first version of the NLP algorithm that applied to all networks was developed using knowledge from the pilot studies and these training sets. Iterative improvements followed, incorporating additional training datasets from PPRG, Alliance, and PPRG-Peoria ( n = 400 each), with continuous review by subject matter experts. In the validation phase, a gold standard dataset (Gold 1) was created from PPRG ( n = 856), Alliance ( n = 360), and PPRG-Peoria ( n = 284) patients who had 4- or 6-month WCC visits in 2020 to 2022 and had not been included in the training datasets. Each note in the Gold 1 dataset was evaluated by two trained chart reviewers to determine the presence of a peanut recommendation and severe eczema. The NLP algorithm from the training phases was applied to the Gold 1 dataset to assess performance. After evaluating the model performance, further adjustments to the algorithm were made to reduce the number

(Gold 1) was created from PPRG ( n = 856), Alliance ( n = 360), and PPRG-Peoria ( n = 284) patients who had 4- or 6-month WCC visits in 2020 to 2022 and had not been included in the training datasets. Each note in the Gold 1 dataset was evaluated by two trained chart reviewers to determine the presence of a peanut recommendation and severe eczema. The NLP algorithm from the training phases was applied to the Gold 1 dataset to assess performance. After evaluating the model performance, further adjustments to the algorithm were made to reduce the number of false positives and to improve recall for severe eczema. A second validation dataset (Gold 2) was created. Gold 2 was also composed of patients who had 4- or 6-month WCC visits in 2020 to 2022 (PPRG ( n = 216), Alliance ( n = 131), and PPRG-Peoria ( n = 53). Additionally, this dataset was built to include equal numbers of patients with and without eczema diagnosis codes. Eczema and related skin conditions were identified in the problem list data associated with the visit using the following ICD-10 diagnosis codes: atopic dermatitis (L20.8, L20.9, L20.81, L20.82, L20.83, L20.84, L20.89), contact dermatitis (L25.9), seborrheic dermatitis (L21.8, L21.9), and dyshidrotic eczema (L30.1). Two trained chart reviewers determined the presence of peanut recommendations and severe eczema in each note. NLP chart review process During the exploratory and training phases of the NLP development, narrative charts were reviewed by experts to refine the model. However, in the validation phase, a more systematic evaluation of the narrative charts was conducted by trained chart reviewers, including domain experts. These reviewers applied a structured and consistent approach to review the accuracy and reliability of the NLP model, providing a more thorough and rigorous assessment compared to the earlier stages. Results from the chart review were recorded in a project-specific data abstraction form, which was displayed alongside the narrative information from the chart for easy reference. For Gold 2 (not Gold 1), in addition to clinical narrative notes, reviewers were given a yes/no flag based on medication table data, showing whether the child had been prescribed severe eczema medication on-or-before the date of the 4- or 6-month WCC visit note being reviewed. Discrepancies in the chart reviewers’ assessments were resolved by discussion between two members of the study team (co-authors LB and MR). Results Infant characteristics were comparable across the two datasets (Gold 1 versus Gold 2). However, across networks, there was variability in race, ethnicity, and insurance type, owing to the network locations and types. The percent of infants with eczema or related skin conditions at 4- or 6- month WCC visits ranged from 0 to 69%. Few infants had egg allergy at 4- or 6- month WCC visits (0–1%). Infant characteristics are presented in Table . The iterative development process of the rule-based NLP algorithm led to two significant revisions: NLP Algorithm v1 and NLP Algorithm v2. NLP Algorithm v2 was a notable improvement over NLP Algorithm v1, with further refinement of the rules for identifying peanut recommendations and severe eczema. NLP Algorithm v1 was validated on the Gold 1 dataset, and NLP Algorithm v2 was validated on the Gold 2 dataset. The performance of these NLP algorithms for peanut recommendation is summarized in Table . NLP Algorithms v1 and v2 for peanut recommendation performed well in each practice network. In the Gold 1 dataset, NLP Algorithm v1 achieved precision values ranging from 0.82 to 0.99 and recall values ranging from 0.96 to 0.98, indicating its ability to accurately identify true positive cases. In the Gold 2 dataset, NLP Algorithm v2 had precision values ranging from 0.91 to 1 and recall values ranging from 0.63 to 0.98. NLP Algorithm v2 exhibited a higher F-measure in the networks combined, but did not outperform NLP Algorithm v1 in all instances. For example, in the PPRG Peoria dataset, NLP Algorithm v2 had an F-measure of 0.74 (precision = 0.91, recall = 0.63) while NLP Algorithm v1 had an F-measure of 0.89, (precision = 0.82, recall = 0.97). The performance of the NLP algorithms for identifying severe eczema is summarized in Table . Severe eczema was not common among infants; the number of true cases of severe eczema in the Gold 1 and Gold 2 datasets was low ( n = 67 in Gold 1 and n = 12 in Gold 2), with considerable variability across networks. In the Gold 1 dataset, NLP Algorithm v1 achieved an overall precision value of 0.62 and recall value of 0.81, while NLP Algorithm v2 demonstrated an overall precision value of 0.52 and recall of 0.92 in the Gold 2 dataset. The Gold 2 dataset had no true positive severe eczema cases in the PPRG-Peoria network to evaluate. In the Gold 1 dataset,

infants; the number of true cases of severe eczema in the Gold 1 and Gold 2 datasets was low ( n = 67 in Gold 1 and n = 12 in Gold 2), with considerable variability across networks. In the Gold 1 dataset, NLP Algorithm v1 achieved an overall precision value of 0.62 and recall value of 0.81, while NLP Algorithm v2 demonstrated an overall precision value of 0.52 and recall of 0.92 in the Gold 2 dataset. The Gold 2 dataset had no true positive severe eczema cases in the PPRG-Peoria network to evaluate. In the Gold 1 dataset, NLP Algorithm v1 for identifying severe eczema demonstrated varied performance across different networks. While it exhibited high specificity and negative predictive value (NPV), indicating its ability to accurately identify true negative cases, its precision and recall were lower. For instance, in the PPRG network, the algorithm achieved a precision of 0.51 and recall of 0.84, resulting in an F-measure of 0.64. In the Alliance network, the F-measure, precision, and recall were all 0.64. In the PPRG-Peoria network, the algorithm achieved a higher F-measure of 0.88 with a precision of 0.90 and recall of 0.86. NLP Algorithm v2, in the networks combined, had higher recall and lower precision. In the PPRG network, Algorithm v2 achieved a precision of 0.64 and a recall of 1, resulting in a higher F-measure of 0.78. However, in the Alliance network, the algorithm showed lower precision (0.44) and recall (0.8), resulting in a lower F-measure of 0.57 than in Algorithm v1. In post-processing, structured data from the iREACH CDS system was used to enhance performance. Specifically, we incorporated the peanut recommendation and severe eczema CDS flags (if a clinician had entered that a peanut recommendation was made this visit or previously, or if a clinician had entered that the patient had severe eczema). This CDS data was not displayed to the reviewers. The NLP model’s performance in the analyses that integrated the CDS flags is detailed in the Appendix Tables and . This CDS-enhanced version of the NLP was used in the iREACH randomized clinical trial analyses. A manual review of the actual iREACH trial cohort’s clinical notes was conducted to ensure the highest level of accuracy and reliability for severe eczema in the analyses in the trial. While automated NLP processes can handle large volumes of data efficiently, manual review allowed for a more thorough examination of the results, to help to identify situations or nuances that automated NLP approaches missed. This approach provided an added layer of validation in the iREACH trial. Discussion In this study, two NLP algorithms were developed to identify (a) peanut recommendations and (b) severe eczema as characterized by pediatric clinicians in clinical notes. Through iterative refinement, two high-performing iterations of these algorithms were crafted, which were subsequently validated in expert-reviewed datasets. Both algorithms performed well on identifying peanut recommendation and were considered acceptable to use in the iREACH trial. The rare occurrence of severe eczema was more difficult to discern using NLP. Therefore, to finalize the analytic data for the trial, the study team manually reviewed all clinical notes that had an NLP indication of possible severe eczema, based on NLP algorithm v2. The study findings demonstrate success in identifying peanut recommendations. The pipeline performed well enough to apply to the large corpus of 4- and 6-month WCC visit notes of 18,480 infants in the iREACH trial. Considering the volume of notes in the trial, an NLP approach was the only viable solution to identify visits at which pediatric clinicians recommended the introduction of peanut products. The successful development of an NLP pipeline to extract this recommendation is a primary contribution of this study which can be replicated in other pragmatic clinical trials. However, identifying cases of severe eczema posed significant challenges, as reflected by lower performance metrics. It is important to consider that the prevalence of eczema among all children is estimated to be 13%, with severe eczema estimated to be 7% of all eczema cases [ ]. Therefore, the rarity of severe eczema in the Gold 1 and 2 datasets was expected. Also, severe eczema is much more complex as a concept than peanut recommendation is. Some patients have severe skin manifestations at one visit but respond swiftly to treatment and have only mild disease at a subsequent visit. Although the performance metrics suggested that the trial results should not rely exclusively on the NLP algorithm, the NLP approach was helpful in identifying infants with possible severe eczema, which prompted further manual chart reviews to exclude false positives. Variability in clinical practice across different networks presents a significant challenge in consistently identifying and treating severe eczema. There appears to be a lack of consensus among pediatric clinicians on how to define severe eczema, possibly stemming from differences

patients have severe skin manifestations at one visit but respond swiftly to treatment and have only mild disease at a subsequent visit. Although the performance metrics suggested that the trial results should not rely exclusively on the NLP algorithm, the NLP approach was helpful in identifying infants with possible severe eczema, which prompted further manual chart reviews to exclude false positives. Variability in clinical practice across different networks presents a significant challenge in consistently identifying and treating severe eczema. There appears to be a lack of consensus among pediatric clinicians on how to define severe eczema, possibly stemming from differences in interpreting clinical guidelines or the inherent complexity of the condition itself. This variability is consistent with a previous study of resident physicians that demonstrated inconsistency in assessing eczema severity [ ]. Therefore, establishing consensus on diagnostic criteria (such as by using a Validated Investigator Global Assessment for Atopic Dermatitis (vIGA-AD) [ ]) and on treatment strategies is essential for ensuring optimal patient care across diverse healthcare settings. The variability in clinical practice and its documentation may have contributed to differences in the performance of NLP across the networks. NLP algorithms also can inherit biases present in the source data, leading to outputs with less accuracy for certain patient groups. Data may reflect persistent racial and ethnic disparities in the diagnosis of eczema and treatment of severe eczema [ – ]. There is an understanding in the field that the diagnosis of eczema needs to better encompass patients of all “shades of skin.” [ ] For this reason, a picture-based vIGA-AD scorecard was developed that reflected diverse skin tones and was provided to clinicians in the intervention arm of the iREACH trial; [ ] nevertheless, there may have been differences in eczema diagnoses across skin tones in both arms of the iREACH trial, which may have created biases within the clinical notes data used by the NLP. Other differences in clinical note writing across networks also pose a challenge for rule-based NLP algorithms. While rule-based NLP has been used in many studies to extract information from clinical notes, its rigid structure may have difficulty accommodating diverse formatting. Clinical notes also may contain language and terminology that vary significantly between different specialties or institutions [ , ]. To address this limitation, more advanced methods such as large language models (LLM) offer promising alternatives. LLMs have demonstrated superior adaptability to variations in text formatting and language usage, which makes them better suited to navigate the complexities of clinical notes sourced from diverse healthcare settings. There are several other limitations of this study. First, the use of NLP to measure the iREACH outcomes was based on the assumption that clinicians document clinical recommendations to patients in progress notes. A recommendation to the parent/caregiver to introduce peanut products may not always be documented by a clinician. Additionally, the CDS in the EHR made it easier to document peanut recommendations in the intervention group. Opportunities for documentation also differed between Epic a nd Centricity EHR systems. The structure of Centricity, with its “obs” terms (succinct text in named data elements that had to be compiled by the project team into narrative style notes), seemed to offer Alliance clinicians fewer opportunities to document in narrative form. Therefore, peanut recommendations and severe eczema were more likely to be identified among intervention patients in Alliance. Conclusions Further research is warranted, especially in the identification of severe eczema, to improve and validate NLP findings and to explore the potential benefits of adopting an NLP algorithm in clinical practice. Overall, this study demonstrates the utility of an NLP approach in helping measure clinical trial outcomes in pragmatic studies. chunks.content: Lichen sclerosus Der Lichen sclerosus (LS; ehem. Lichen sclerosus et atrophicus) ist eine chronisch entzündliche Dermatose multifaktorieller Genese, deren Ätiologie bislang nicht vollständig geklärt ist. Die Prävalenz wird auf etwa 0,1–0,3 % bei beiden Geschlechtern geschätzt, jedoch bis 0,7 % bei Frauen über 65 Jahren [ ]. Aufgrund unspezifischer Symptome, Tabuisierung und Scham-assoziierter Krankheitsvermeidung sowie oligosymptomatischen bis asymptomatischen Verläufen (ca. 30 % der Fälle) ist jedoch von einer deutlich höheren Dunkelziffer auszugehen. In etwa 85 % der Fälle ist der Befall auf die Genitalregion beschränkt, extragenitale Manifestationen sind selten. Bei beiden Geschlechtern kommt es neben Juckreiz häufig zu Brennen, Erythemen, Erosionen und im Verlauf zu sklerotischen Veränderungen mit Narbenbildung und Verwachsungen. Klinisch präsentiert sich der LS initial typischerweise mit starkem Pruritus und flachen, weißlich-elfenbeinfarbenen, wachsartigen Makulae, die konfluieren und zu atrophen, gefältelten oder – seltener – hyperkeratotischen Plaques übergehen können. Geschlechtsspezifisch zeigen sich bei Frauen periklitorale Schwellungen, Fissuren, Ekchymosen, und es kommt bei fortschreitendem Verlauf häufig zum Verlust der kleinen Schamlippen und der Klitorisvorhaut (Abb. a). Bei Männern hingegen sind v. a. Glans und Präputium betroffen (Abb. b), typischerweise mit porzellanartig weißlichen, sklerotischen Narben, die Phimose, Verwachsungen oder ein sklerotisches Frenulum breve begünstigen. Bei beiden Geschlechtern können Verwachsungen und anatomische Veränderungen zu urogenitalen Symptomen und sexuellen Dysfunktionen wie Dyspareunien, schmerzhaften Erektionen und Anorgasmie führen. Wichtig ist zu beachten, dass LS eine fakultative Präkanzerose darstellt: Bis zu 4 % der Betroffenen entwickeln nichtmelanozytäre Karzinome der Haut, überwiegend Plattenepithelkarzinome [ ]. Eine frühzeitige Diagnose und adäquate Therapie sind daher essenziell. Die Diagnose des LS erfolgt meist klinisch und kann in unklaren Fällen oder bei Verdacht auf Malignität durch eine Biopsie ergänzt werden. Differenzialdiagnostisch kommen der Lichen planus – hier v. a. die erosive Form –, Ekzeme sowie in bestimmten Fällen auch eine genitale Vitiligo infrage. Lichen sclerosus stellt eine fakultative Präkanzerose dar Ziel der Behandlung ist die Kontrolle der Erkrankung und Linderung der Symptome, insbesondere Heilung von Fissuren und Erosionen und Reduktion der Sklerose. Erstlinientherapie sind hochpotente topische Glukokortikoide (Klasse III–IV, Clobetasolpropionat 0,05 % Salbe oder Mometasonfuroat 0,1 % Salbe), die 1‑ bis 2‑mal täglich über bis zu 3 Monate aufgetragen werden, gefolgt von einer Erhaltungsphase in längeren Intervallen zur Rezidivprophylaxe. Ein Standardschema existiert gemäß Leitlinie nicht. Bei Unverträglichkeit oder unzureichendem Ansprechen können (additiv) topische Calcineurininhibitoren (Tacrolimus oder Pimecrolimus) „off-label“ eingesetzt werden. Begleitend werden 2‑mal täglich topische Emollienzien zur Basispflege und die Vermeidung von Triggerfaktoren (Reibung, Nässe) dringend empfohlen. In schweren therapierefraktären Fällen kann unter Beachtung der Teratogenität eine Therapie mit systemischen Retinoiden (Acitretin 20–30 mg) oder eine systemische Immunsuppression initiiert werden (Methotrexat 10–15 mg/Woche), wobei die Evidenzlage für Systemtherapien insgesamt schwach ist. Eine frühzeitige operative Sanierung mittels Zirkumzision ist bei männlichen Patienten mit Befall des Präputiums indiziert, bei Verengungen der Harnröhre bzw. Meatusstenose die Urethroplastik und Meatusplastik. Im Spätstadium stellt auch bei Frauen die chirurgische Sanierung eine weitere Behandlungsoption dar, die bei Synechien der Labien oder Verengung des Orificium externum der Urethra indiziert sein kann [ ]. Lichen planus mucosae Der Lichen planus (LP) ist die prototypische lichenoide Dermatitis und eine nichtinfektiöse, entzündliche Erkrankung von Haut und Schleimhäuten. Klinisch dominieren starker Pruritus und charakteristische, flache, polygonale Papeln. Die Prävalenz beträgt etwa 1 %, Frauen sind häufiger betroffen als Männer [ ]. Am häufigsten manifestiert sich der LP an den Schleimhäuten (auch Lichen planus mucosae), v. a. enoral, jedoch tritt ein genitaler Befall nicht selten auf [ ]. Bei Männern zeigt sich der genitale LP überwiegend in der klassischen Form mit rosafarbenen bis violetten glänzenden Papeln an Eichel und Sulcus coronarius (Abb. c). Erosive Veränderungen sind seltener, können jedoch Schmerzen, Dysurie und Vernarbungen verursachen. Bei Frauen dominiert hingegen die erosive Form mit glasigen, erythematösen bis violetten Läsionen mit hyperkeratotischem Rand, typischerweise an Vestibulum, kleinen Schamlippen und Vagina. Im Verlauf können Vernarbungen, Synechien und Einengungen des Scheideneingangs entstehen, was Dyspareunie und sexuelle Dysfunktion zur Folge haben kann. Seltener treten papulosquamöse oder hypertrophe Formen auf. Chronisch erosive oder hypertrophe Verläufe können, ähnlich wie beim LS, zu Narbenbildung, anatomischen Veränderungen und funktionellen Einschränkungen führen. Der LP mucosae gilt, im Gegensatz zur rein kutanen Form, als Präkanzerose mit einem Lebenszeitrisiko von etwa 2 % für die Entwicklung von Plattenepithelkarzinomen, was ein langfristiges Monitoring der Betroffenen erforderlich macht [ ]. Die Diagnose des LP wird primär klinisch gestellt, kann jedoch histologisch abgesichert werden. Vor allem bei der erosiven Form sollten differenzialdiagnostisch aphthöse Erkrankungen, bullöse Autoimmundermatosen (Pemphigus vulgaris, Schleimhautpemphigoid) sowie infektiöse Ursachen wie genitale Herpesinfektionen und Kandidosen sowie Syphilis, Ulcus molle und Lymphogranuloma venereum ausgeschlossen werden. Die Diagnose des Lichen planus mucosae wird primär klinisch gestellt Therapeutisch stehen beim genitalen LP die Linderung der Symptome und die Eindämmung der Entzündung im Vordergrund. Mittel der ersten Wahl sind mittel- bis hochpotente topische Glukokortikoide, die über mehrere Wochen täglich und anschließend in Erhaltungsintervallen appliziert werden. Bei unzureichendem Ansprechen oder Unverträglichkeiten können topische Calcineurininhibitoren („off-label“) eingesetzt werden. In schweren oder therapierefraktären

gestellt, kann jedoch histologisch abgesichert werden. Die Diagnose des Lichen planus mucosae wird primär klinisch gestellt Therapeutisch stehen beim genitalen LP die Linderung der Symptome und die Eindämmung der Entzündung im Vordergrund. Mittel der ersten Wahl sind mittel- bis hochpotente topische Glukokortikoide, die über mehrere Wochen täglich und anschließend in Erhaltungsintervallen appliziert werden. Bei unzureichendem Ansprechen oder Unverträglichkeiten können topische Calcineurininhibitoren („off-label“) eingesetzt werden. In schweren oder therapierefraktären Fällen kann eine systemische Therapie mit Kortikosteroiden, Retinoiden oder eine immunsuppressive Therapie (Cyclosporin 3–10 mg/kg/Tag; „second line“: Azathioprin, Hydroxychloroquin, Methotrexat, Mycophenolatmofetil) erforderlich sein. Ergänzend sind in ausgewählten Situationen chirurgische Maßnahmen indiziert, insbesondere bei funktionellen Einschränkungen [ , ]. Psoriasis inversa Die Psoriasis vulgaris ist eine chronisch entzündliche Hauterkrankung, die etwa 2 % der europäischen und nordamerikanischen Bevölkerung betrifft und meist in ihrer typischen Form, der chronischen Plaquepsoriasis, auftritt. Die Psoriasis inversa (PI) stellt dabei keine eigenständige Entität dar, sondern ein lokalisiertes Auftreten der Psoriasis vorwiegend oder ausschließlich in intertriginösen Arealen. Die Prävalenz der PI bei Personen mit Psoriasis wird je nach Studie mit bis zu 30 % angegeben [ ]. Die Plaquepsoriasis präsentiert sich typischerweise mit gut abgrenzbaren, erythematösen, silbrig schuppenden Plaques, die bevorzugt an Ellenbogen, Knien, Sakralregion und Kopfhaut auftreten. Im Gegensatz zeigen sich die Plaques im Bereich der intertriginösen Areale (axillär, submammär, Labien, Skrotum, Analfalte) klinisch weniger induriert, nässend, mit fehlender oder nur minimaler oberflächlicher Schuppung und häufig mazeriert (Abb. d). Die Diagnose der PI erfolgt in erster Linie klinisch und histologisch, zudem kann aber eine mikrobielle Abklärung notwendig sein, um klinisch ähnliche Differenzialdiagnosen (Tinea corporis, Kandidose, Intertrigo) auszuschließen und bakterielle Superinfektionen bei PI gezielt zu behandeln. Die Behandlung der PI ist aufgrund des warmen, feuchten Milieus der Hautfalten anspruchsvoll. Zwar erleichtert die geringere Hornschicht intertriginöser Areale die Penetration topischer Medikamente, gleichzeitig steigt jedoch das Risiko für unerwünschte Nebenwirkungen wie Irritationen und Atrophie, insbesondere bei Anwendung hochpotenter Kortikosteroide. Topische Therapien umfassen daher niedrig- bis mittelpotente Kortikosteroide, Calcipotriol und „off-label“ Calcineurininhibitoren, die sich bei der PI als wirksam erwiesen haben und keine Atrophie verursachen. Ergänzend empfehlen sich Emollienzien, Zinksalben, Trockenhalten betroffener Regionen sowie bei Bedarf antibiotische oder antimykotische Maßnahmen. Bei therapieresistenter PI sollte frühzeitig eine systemische Behandlung mit konventionellen Systemtherapeutika (Fumarate, Methotrexat) oder Biologika gemäß Leitlinien der Plaquepsoriasis erwogen werden. Eine Beteiligung des Genitalbereichs stellt hier ein sog. Upgrade-Kriterium dar, aufgrund dessen bereits bei geringem BSA-Befall eine Systemtherapie indiziert ist [ ]. Auch wenn die direkte Studienlage in Bezug zur PI schwach ist, zeigen kleinere Fallserien eine vergleichbare Ansprechrate zur Plaquepsoriasis [ ]. Hidradenitis suppurativa Die Hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) ist eine chronisch rezidivierende, entzündliche Hauterkrankung multifaktorieller Genese. Pathophysiologisch steht eine follikuläre Okklusion im Vordergrund, begünstigt durch genetische Prädisposition, immunologische Dysregulation sowie verschiedene äußere Einflüsse. Die enge Assoziation mit Adipositas und Nikotinkonsum unterstreicht die Bedeutung externer Risikofaktoren [ , ]. Betroffene leiden häufig unter erheblichem psychosozialem Leidensdruck, und es bestehen Assoziationen mit multiplen Komorbiditäten wie Diabetes mellitus, Atherosklerose und chronisch entzündlichen Darmerkrankungen. Die Assoziation mit Adipositas und Nikotinkonsum unterstreicht die Bedeutung externer Risikofaktoren Klinisch manifestiert sich die Erkrankung durch schmerzhafte, entzündliche Knoten, Abszesse und Fistelgänge, die bevorzugt in intertriginösen und apokrindrüsenreichen Arealen auftreten, insbesondere Axillae, Inguinal- und Perianalregion, submammär sowie im Gesäßbereich (Abb. e). Die chronische Inflammation kann zu Erosionen, Ulzerationen, fibrotischen Plaques und hypertrophen Narben führen sowie bei längerem Krankheitsverlauf zur Bildung von epithelialisierten Tunneln. Die Diagnose wird klinisch gestellt und anhand der International Hidradenitis Suppurativa Severity Score System (IHS)4-Kriterien (Tab. ) in milde, moderate/mittelschwere und schwere Verlaufsformen eingestuft. Differenzialdiagnostisch sollten bei untypischem Erscheinungsbild Furunkulosen sowie abszessbildende Infektionen anderer Genese ausgeschlossen werden (z. B. kutane MRSA-Infektionen oder atypische Mykobakteriosen). Bei bestehender Grunderkrankung ist zudem an eine – gegebenenfalls fistulierende – kutane Manifestation eines Morbus Crohn zu denken. Die Therapie richtet sich nach Schwere- und Entzündungsgrad, Grundlage ist jedoch stets die Empfehlung zur Gewichtsreduktion und Nikotinkarenz, sofern zutreffend. Bei milder aktiver HS (IHS4 1–3) kommen topische Antibiotika wie Clindamycin Gel 2-mal täglich sowie topische Antiseptika zum Einsatz. Bei moderat bis schwerer aktiver HS (IHS4 ≥ 4) ist eine systemische Therapie indiziert. Initial wird eine orale antibiotische Therapie über maximal 12 Wochen mit Doxycyclin 2 × 100 mg/d oder alternativ eine Kombinationstherapie mit Clindamycin 2 × 300 mg/d und Rifampicin 2 × 300 mg/d empfohlen. Bei therapierefraktärer oder schwerer HS stehen zudem Biologika zur Verfügung, insbesondere die aus der Psoriasistherapie bekannten TNF-α-Inhibitoren, Interleukin(IL)-17A-Inhibitoren sowie IL-17A/F-Inhibitoren, die in höherer Frequenz oder Dosierung als für die Plaquepsoriasis verabreicht werden. Weitere Substanzen befinden sich in klinischer Prüfung. In inaktiven (nichtentzündlichen) Intervallen und/oder bei ausgeprägter Fistelbildung ist eine chirurgische Sanierung in der Regel indiziert, um persistierende Läsionen zu entfernen [ ]. Ekzeme Genitale Ekzeme stellen einen häufigen dermatologischen Vorstellungsgrund dar, wobei insbesondere die atopische Dermatitis

Wochen mit Doxycyclin 2 × 100 mg/d oder alternativ eine Kombinationstherapie mit Clindamycin 2 × 300 mg/d und Rifampicin 2 × 300 mg/d empfohlen. Bei therapierefraktärer oder schwerer HS stehen zudem Biologika zur Verfügung, insbesondere die aus der Psoriasistherapie bekannten TNF-α-Inhibitoren, Interleukin(IL)-17A-Inhibitoren sowie IL-17A/F-Inhibitoren, die in höherer Frequenz oder Dosierung als für die Plaquepsoriasis verabreicht werden. Weitere Substanzen befinden sich in klinischer Prüfung. In inaktiven (nichtentzündlichen) Intervallen und/oder bei ausgeprägter Fistelbildung ist eine chirurgische Sanierung in der Regel indiziert, um persistierende Läsionen zu entfernen [ ]. Ekzeme Genitale Ekzeme stellen einen häufigen dermatologischen Vorstellungsgrund dar, wobei insbesondere die atopische Dermatitis (AD) und die allergische oder irritativ-toxische Kontaktdermatitis differenzialdiagnostisch von Relevanz sind. Die AD ist eine chronisch entzündliche, immunvermittelte Dermatose mit multifaktorieller Pathogenese, in deren Entstehung genetische Prädisposition, epidermale Barrierestörung, immunologische Dysregulation sowie Umweltfaktoren involviert sind. Die Prävalenz zeigt sich in den letzten Jahrzehnten steigend und beträgt bis zu 20 % der Kinder und etwa 10 % der Erwachsenen [ ]. Klinisch imponieren stark juckende, erythematös-ödematöse, unscharf begrenzte Ekzemherde, die Papeln, Vesikel, Krusten- oder Schuppenbildung aufweisen können und bei chronischem Kratzen exkoriiert oder lichenifiziert sein können. Typischerweise manifestieren sich die Läsionen in den klassischen Prädilektionsarealen (Kopf-Hals-Region, Beugen, Hände und Füße); eine Genitalbeteiligung ist jedoch ebenfalls möglich (Abb. a). Die Kontaktdermatitis hingegen resultiert aus exogenen Noxen, entweder im Sinne einer irritativen/toxischen oder einer allergischen Reaktion, und präsentiert sich mit lokalisierten, häufig pruriginösen Ekzemen, die bei entsprechender Exposition auch genital auftreten können (Abb. b). Ebenfalls dem Formenkreis der Ekzeme zuzuordnen ist der perianale Lichen simplex chronicus als Sonderform des Lichen simplex chronicus. Dabei handelt es sich um sekundäre Hautveränderungen, die infolge rezidivierender mechanischer Manipulation bei chronischem Pruritus im Sinne eines Juck-Kratz-Teufelskreises entstehen. Klinisch manifestieren sich diese meist als perianale, scharf begrenzte, ekzematöse bis lichenoide Plaques, bei längerem Bestehen auch als hyperkeratotische oder noduläre, prurigoartige Veränderungen. Die Ursachen des perianalen Pruritus sind vielfältig, häufig liegen jedoch irritative Intimpflege, Hämorrhoidalleiden, feuchtes Milieu oder eine atopische Diathese zugrunde. Bei Verdacht auf eine allergische Kontaktdermatitis kann eine allergologische Testung sinnvoll sein Die Diagnosestellung erfolgt primär klinisch und mittels bakteriologischer Diagnostik zum Ausschluss allfälliger Superinfektionen. Bei Verdacht auf eine allergische Kontaktdermatitis kann eine allergologische Testung (Epikutantests) sinnvoll sein. Therapeutisch stehen die Elimination exogener Triggerfaktoren (z. B. Desinfektionsmittel, Duftstoffe, Latex, lokale chemische Kontrazeptiva) sowie eine konsequente Basistherapie mit Emollienzien im Vordergrund. Leichte bis moderate Läsionen sprechen in der Regel auf eine kurzzeitige Behandlung mit topischen Glukokortikosteroiden oder alternativ Calcineurininhibitoren an. Systemische Therapien sind bei isoliert genitaler Manifestation in der Regel nicht erforderlich und sollten lediglich in ausgewählten Einzelfällen erwogen werden [ , ]. Beim perianalen Lichen simplex chronicus steht die konsequente Vermeidung des Kratzens im Vordergrund. Kurzfristige topische Kortikosteroidtherapien können dabei helfen, den Juck-Kratz-Teufelskreis zu durchbrechen. Therapierbare Ursachen des Pruritus (z. B. Hämorrhoiden) sollten gezielt mitbehandelt werden. Fixes Arzneimittelexanthem Hautreaktionen zählen zu den häufigsten unerwünschten Arzneimittelwirkungen. Eine besondere Form stellt das fixe Arzneimittelexanthem (AZME) dar, eine Typ-IV-Hypersensitivitätsreaktion, die typischerweise innerhalb von 48 h nach Exposition auftritt und sowohl Haut als auch (Genital‑)Schleimhäute betreffen kann. Klinisch zeigen sich solitäre scharf begrenzte, runde bis ovale erythematöse oder livide Makulae, häufig mit zentraler Hyperpigmentierung, seltener mit bullöser Komponente oder Streuung (multilokuläres fixes AZME). Als prototypische Reaktion hautresidenter T‑Zellen rezidiviert das fixe AZME bei Re-Exposition charakteristischerweise in loco. Eine genitale Beteiligung (Mukosa der Glans penis oder Vulva) ist dabei häufig, v. a. bei Männern, und wird in der Literatur in bis zu 30 % der Fälle beschrieben. Zu den häufigsten Auslösern eines fixen AZME zählen Analgetika (insbesondere NSAR und Paracetamol) sowie Antibiotika (v. a. Cotrimoxazol) [ , ]. Die Diagnose erfolgt klinisch und in Zusammenschau mit der Anamnese. Gelegentlich kann eine allergologische In-loco-Patch-Testung ein positives Ergebnis erzielen. Therapeutisch stehen die Identifikation und das Absetzen des auslösenden Medikaments im Vordergrund. Bei milden bis moderaten Verläufen kann eine kurzzeitige topische Therapie mit Glukokortikoiden sowie ggf. die Gabe von Antihistaminika zur Symptomlinderung erfolgen [ , ]. Morbus Behçet Der Morbus Behçet ist eine inflammatorische Multisystemerkrankung unklarer Ätiologie mit sowohl autoinflammatorischen als auch autoimmunologischen Merkmalen. Pathogenetisch zählt sie zu den MHC-I-assoziierten Erkrankungen, wobei insbesondere HLA-B51 und HLA-A26 prädisponierend wirken. Histologisch findet sich typischerweise eine leukozytoklastische Vaskulitis mit neutrophilen Infiltraten, Endothelschädigung und fibrinoider Nekrose. Die Erkrankung tritt weltweit auf, zeigt jedoch eine deutlich höhere Prävalenz entlang der historischen „Seidenstraße“, insbesondere in der Türkei, im Nahen Osten und in Fernost-Asien, mit Raten von bis zu 300 pro 100.000 Einwohner, während sie in Mitteleuropa mit weniger als 1 pro 100.000 deutlich seltener ist [ , ]. Klinisch zeigt sich der Morbus Behçet mit rezidivierenden, schmerzhaften oralen und genitalen Aphthen sowie kutanen Läsionen als Leitsymptom (Abb. c und d ). Die Aphthen sind oft multipel, mit grauweißer Pseudomembran und von einem erythematösem Randsaum begrenzt. Kleine Läsionen heilen narbenlos ab, größere Aphthen können ulzerieren und narbig abheilen. Die genitalen Ulzera stellen nach den oralen Aphthen das zweithäufigste klinische Symptom dar und präsentieren

„Seidenstraße“, insbesondere in der Türkei, im Nahen Osten und in Fernost-Asien, mit Raten von bis zu 300 pro 100.000 Einwohner, während sie in Mitteleuropa mit weniger als 1 pro 100.000 deutlich seltener ist [ , ]. Klinisch zeigt sich der Morbus Behçet mit rezidivierenden, schmerzhaften oralen und genitalen Aphthen sowie kutanen Läsionen als Leitsymptom (Abb. c und d ). Die Aphthen sind oft multipel, mit grauweißer Pseudomembran und von einem erythematösem Randsaum begrenzt. Kleine Läsionen heilen narbenlos ab, größere Aphthen können ulzerieren und narbig abheilen. Die genitalen Ulzera stellen nach den oralen Aphthen das zweithäufigste klinische Symptom dar und präsentieren sich als ausgestanzte, stark schmerzhafte Ulzera mit fibrinösem Exsudat an der Basis, die eine starke Ähnlichkeit zu syphilitischen Primäraffekten aufweisen können. Bei Männern finden sie sich überwiegend skrotal, während sie bei Frauen häufiger an den Labien lokalisiert sind. Der Morbus Behçet ist eine inflammatorische Multisystemerkrankung Zusätzlich können gastrointestinale, vaskuläre, neurologische, artikuläre und okuläre Manifestationen (Retinitis, Uveitis) auftreten, die den multisystemischen Charakter der Erkrankung unterstreichen. Da pathognomonische Labor- oder Bildgebungsbefunde fehlen, erfolgt die Diagnosestellung klinisch anhand internationaler Kriterien (Tab. ). Unterstützend können ein positiver Pathergietest sowie die Bestimmung prädisponierender HLA-Antigene (z. B. HLA-B51) herangezogen werden [ ]. Differenzialdiagnostisch kommen insbesondere eine rezidivierende Aphthose sowie ein Morbus Crohn mit oraler oder genitaler Beteiligung in Betracht, ferner auch blasenbildende Autoimmundermatosen. Bei jungen Patientinnen mit akut auftretenden, schmerzhaften genitalen Ulzera ist das Ulcus vulvae acutum (Lipschütz-Ulkus) als wichtige Differenzialdiagnose zu bedenken. Vor allem bei Erstmanifestationen oder gleichzeitig bestehenden systemischen Symptomen sollten eine Herpes-simplex-Erstinfektionen, Medikamentenreaktionen (Stevens-Johnson-Syndrom) oder eine reaktive Arthritis ausgeschlossen werden. Die Therapie richtet sich nach dem Schweregrad und Organbefall und erfolgt gemäß den aktuellen European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR)-Empfehlungen. Leichte mukokutane Manifestationen werden in der Regel topisch mit Antiseptika, lokalanästhetischen Externa oder lokalen Glukokortikoiden behandelt. Bei schwerer Symptomatik können kurzzeitig systemische Glukokortikoide angewandt werden. Bei moderaten bis schweren Verlaufsformen oder häufigen Rezidiven ist eine systemische immunsuppressive/-modulatorische Therapie indiziert, deren Auswahl sich nach den Leitsymptomen, Patientenmerkmalen und betroffenen Organsystemen richtet. Therapeutische Optionen umfassen Colchicin, Azathioprin, Thalidomid, Interferon‑α, Dapson, TNF-α-Inhibitoren sowie Phosphodiesterase-4-Inhibitoren (z. B. Apremilast) [ ]. Plasmazellbalanitis (Zoon-Balanitis) Die Plasmazellbalanitis (PZB) ist eine chronische, idiopathische, reaktive Balanoposthitis, die überwiegend bei unbeschnittenen älteren Männern auftritt und vermutlich sekundär infolge einer Vorhautdysfunktion entsteht, häufig im Zusammenhang mit Mikrotraumata und unzureichender Hygiene. Eine Dysfunktion des Präputiums begünstigt die Retention von Wärme, Smegma und Feuchtigkeit und erhöht dadurch die Anfälligkeit für sekundäre Infektionen. Typischerweise manifestiert sich die PZB an Vorhaut und Eichel als symmetrische, scharf begrenzte, erythematöse, glänzende Plaques mit feinen roten Punkten, den charakteristischen „Cayennepfefferflecken“ (Abb. b). Im Gegensatz zu anderen entzündlichen genitalen Dermatosen gilt die PZB nicht als Präkanzerose, sollte jedoch histologisch abgeklärt werden, um Malignome mit ähnlichem Erscheinungsbild, insbesondere den extramammären Morbus Paget oder die Erythroplasie de Queyrat, auszuschließen [ ]. Therapeutisch kommen Behandlungen mit Calcineurininhibitoren, Kortikosteroiden oder 2 % Mupirocin-Salbe über mehrere Wochen zur Anwendung. Chronisch rezidivierende Verläufe sind jedoch häufig. In diesen Fällen bleibt die Zirkumzision die Therapie der Wahl, die in der Regel zu einer vollständigen und anhaltenden Remission führt [ ]. Ergänzend ist stets eine Schulung zur genitalen Hygiene empfehlenswert. Wenngleich deutlich seltener, existiert ein analoges Krankheitsbild bei Frauen, bekannt als Plasmazellvulvitis oder Zoon-Vulvitis. Klinisch präsentiert sie sich mit rötlich-braunen, glänzenden Plaques an den Labien oder der Klitoris sowie ebenfalls fein punktförmigen Erythemen (Cayennepfefferflecken). Diagnostik und Lokaltherapie entsprechen weitgehend jenen der Plasmazellbalanitis. Ulcus vulvae acutum (Lipschütz-Ulkus) Das Ulcus vulvae acutum ist eine sehr seltene, vermutlich unterdiagnostizierte Erkrankung, die durch das plötzliche Auftreten schmerzhafter, nekrotischer Ulzera der Vulva charakterisiert ist. Betroffen sind nahezu ausschließlich (> 90 %) junge Frauen unter 20 Jahren, typischerweise unabhängig von vorangegangenem Sexualkontakt [ ]. Die Ätiologie ist bislang nicht vollständig geklärt. Vermutet wird eine postinfektiöse Hypersensibilitäts- oder immunvermittelte Reaktion, häufig im Anschluss an eine Primärinfektion mit Epstein-Barr-Virus (EBV). Auch andere Infektionserreger wie u. a. Zytomegalievirus (CMV), Mycoplasma pneumoniae , Mumpsvirus wurden im Zusammenhang beschrieben. Das Ulcus vulvae acutum kann solitär oder multipel auftreten und ist meist an den Labiae minorae lokalisiert, seltener an den großen Labien (Abb. a) oder dem Perineum. Charakteristisch sind dabei stark schmerzhafte, scharf begrenzte, tief ulzerierte und durch fibrinöse Beläge oder gräuliches Exsudat gekennzeichnete Läsionen. Die Diagnose wird klinisch und als Ausschlussdiagnose gestellt, nachdem sexuell übertragbare Infektionen (insbesondere Herpesinfektion, Ulcus durum und Ulcus molle) sowie andere ulzerative Erkrankungen wie der Morbus Behçet, aphthöse Ulzera, traumatische Läsionen und medikamenteninduzierte Reaktionen ausgeschlossen wurden. Das Ulcus vulvae acutum ist in der Regel selbstlimitierend und heilt innerhalb von 2 bis 3 Wochen spontan ab. Rezidive sind selten, jedoch in Zusammenhang mit erneuten Infektionen beschrieben. Die Therapie ist daher vorwiegend symptomatisch und zielt auf Schmerzlinderung sowie die Vermeidung sekundärer Infektionen ab. Topische Anästhetika und orale Analgetika können zur Schmerzkontrolle eingesetzt werden. Topische Glukokortikoide können die Abheilung beschleunigen – systemische Glukokortikoide sollten nur in ausgewählten Fällen in Betracht gezogen werden [ ]. Antibiotika sind nur bei nachgewiesenen

und Ulcus molle) sowie andere ulzerative Erkrankungen wie der Morbus Behçet, aphthöse Ulzera, traumatische Läsionen und medikamenteninduzierte Reaktionen ausgeschlossen wurden. Das Ulcus vulvae acutum ist in der Regel selbstlimitierend und heilt innerhalb von 2 bis 3 Wochen spontan ab. Rezidive sind selten, jedoch in Zusammenhang mit erneuten Infektionen beschrieben. Die Therapie ist daher vorwiegend symptomatisch und zielt auf Schmerzlinderung sowie die Vermeidung sekundärer Infektionen ab. Topische Anästhetika und orale Analgetika können zur Schmerzkontrolle eingesetzt werden. Topische Glukokortikoide können die Abheilung beschleunigen – systemische Glukokortikoide sollten nur in ausgewählten Fällen in Betracht gezogen werden [ ]. Antibiotika sind nur bei nachgewiesenen bakteriellen Sekundärinfektionen indiziert und spielen in der Primärtherapie keine Rolle. Fazit für die Praxis Genitoanale Dermatosen sind häufig, werden jedoch aufgrund unspezifischer Symptome und Tabuisierung oft spät diagnostiziert. Es sollten eine sorgfältige Inspektion, vollständige Anamnese und frühzeitige Biopsie bei therapierefraktären Läsionen erfolgen. Lichen sclerosus und Lichen planus sind wichtige Differenzialdiagnosen mit dem Risiko funktioneller Einschränkungen und (bei LS) potenzieller maligner Entartung: Regelmäßige Kontrollen sind erforderlich. Psoriasis inversa benötigt eine differenzierte topische Therapie; eine frühe Systemtherapie sollte erwogen werden (Genitalbefall als Schweregrad-Upgrade). Die Hidradenitis suppurativa sollte früh erkannt und nach IHS4 eingestuft werden. Lifestyle-Modifikation, Antibiotika und Biologika sollten leitliniengerecht eingesetzt werden. Ekzeme und Kontaktdermatitiden bleiben häufig: Konsequente Triggerelimination und Basistherapie sind zentral. Ulzerierende Erkrankungen (Morbus Behçet, Lipschütz-Ulkus) erfordern ein systematisches Ausschlussverfahren und u. U. eine interdisziplinäre Betreuung. Nicht stigmatisierende Kommunikation und ausführliche Patientenaufklärung verbessern Adhärenz und Langzeitverlauf.

documents.title: BAD guidelines for the management of lichen sclerosus

chunks.content: Background Bladder Pain Syndrome/Interstitial Cystitis (BPS/IC) and vulvodynia are chronic, debilitating conditions characterized by persistent pain localized to the bladder and vulvar regions, respectively. These disorders are particularly prevalent among women of reproductive age and are known to substantially impair daily functioning and overall quality of life (QoL) [ , ]. Conventional management approaches—including pharmacological therapies, behavioral interventions, and pelvic floor physical therapy—frequently result in limited or short-term symptom relief. BPS/IC is defined by ongoing pelvic pain or pressure perceived to originate from the bladder, often accompanied by urinary urgency and increased frequency [ ]. Despite considerable research efforts, the precise pathophysiological mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Current evidence points toward a multifactorial etiology involving urothelial dysfunction, dysregulated immune responses, and neurogenic inflammation, all of which may contribute to the persistence and complexity of symptoms [ ]. In recognition of this clinical complexity, a recent international consensus has identified five major gynecologic comorbidities that frequently coexist with BPS/IC: (1) endometriosis/adenomyosis, (2) genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder, (3) overactive pelvic floor muscles, (4) hormone-associated genitourinary changes, and (5) vulvodynia/vestibulodynia [ ]. These conditions often overlap symptomatically with BPS/IC and may influence both clinical presentation and therapeutic responsiveness. Therefore, a comprehensive assessment that integrates gynecologic findings is now increasingly emphasized in BPS/IC care. In recent years, laser-based therapies have emerged as a promising minimally invasive modality capable of targeting both epithelial and neuromuscular components of pelvic pain syndromes [ – ]. Furthermore, this review considers laser-based treatments for related gynecologic conditions that share symptomatic or mechanistic overlap with BPS/IC—such as vulvar lichen sclerosus and genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) observed in specific populations (e.g., breast cancer survivors) [ – ]. This narrative review summarizes the current body of evidence regarding the use of laser treatment in BPS/IC and vulvodynia, with a focus on therapeutic efficacy, safety profiles, and potential mechanisms of action. Special attention is given to differential treatment responses among patient subgroups, the biological plausibility of tissue remodeling effects, and the pressing need for standardized protocols to guide clinical application. Main Text Vulvodynia and its overlap with BPS/IC: prevalence, pathophysiology, and clinical impact Vulvodynia is defined as persistent vulvar discomfort or pain without a clear identifiable cause, typically lasting for at least three months [ ]. Patients often describe symptoms such as burning, stinging, or irritation, which may be spontaneous or triggered by physical contact [ , ]. The underlying mechanisms are considered multifactorial, involving peripheral nerve sensitization, inflammatory responses, hormonal influences, and genetic predispositions [ – ]. These complex and overlapping factors frequently complicate diagnosis and long-term management. Epidemiological studies have shown that BPS/IC affects approximately 2.7% to 6.5% of women [ , , ], while vulvodynia occurs in around 8% of women by the age of 40 and up to 16% over a lifetime [ , ]. Both conditions are associated with significant reductions in QoL, including impaired sexual function and significant psychological distress [ ]. Gardella et al. reported that among women newly diagnosed with IC, 23.4% experienced spontaneous vulvodynia, and 74.5% reported provoked vulvodynia [ ]. These individuals also exhibited significant sexual dysfunction, with a mean Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI) score of 16.85 ± 8.73, significantly lower than that of healthy controls (27.34 ± 6.41; p < 0.0001). Similarly, the UNICORN-1 study by Okui et al. found that Asian women with BPS/IC had markedly lower FSFI scores (15.72 ± 4.46 vs. 26.3 ± 4.93; p < 0.05) and higher vulvodynia swab test scores than controls [ ]. Notably, a recent international consensus panel has formally recognized vulvodynia/vestibulodynia as one of the five major gynecologic comorbidities associated with BPS/IC, further highlighting the clinical relevance of this overlap [ ]. Cellular and neurological basis Beyond this shared anatomical origin, bladder pain syndrome/interstitial cystitis and vulvodynia also overlap at the cellular and neuroinflammatory levels [ ]. Mast cells are increasingly recognized as key mediators in chronic inflammatory disorders such as BPS/IC and vulvodynia. These immune cells secrete various proinflammatory molecules—including cytokines, neuropeptides, and vasoactive agents—that are implicated in the pathogenesis of stress-related neuroinflammatory conditions [ ]. In BPS/IC, activated mast cells can enhance neural excitability and alter neurotransmitter dynamics, contributing to persistent pelvic pain and urinary dysfunction [ ]. In vulvodynia as well, increased mast cell activation has been observed. Histamine released from these cells is thought to activate peripheral nociceptors such as C-fibers and A-delta fibers, enhancing nociceptive signaling [ , ]. Women with vulvodynia have been shown to exhibit increased pressure pain sensitivity not only in the vulvar area but also at distant body sites, suggesting a role for central sensitization in symptom generation [ ]. Furthermore, patients with provoked vestibulodynia demonstrate impaired diffuse noxious inhibitory control (DNIC), indicating dysfunction in endogenous pain inhibition. These individuals also tend to show globally lowered pain thresholds compared to healthy controls, reflecting a generalized hypersensitivity state [ ]. A recent cross-species study has further advanced our understanding of mast cells by identifying distinct subsets with organ-specific transcriptomic profiles in both mice and humans [ ]. Neurogenic inflammation, neuropathic pain, and central sensitization The involvement of both peripheral and central nervous systems in the pathophysiology of BPS/IC and vulvodynia is intricate and not yet fully elucidated. Clinical findings suggest the presence of subtypes, with pain arising either from peripheral organs or generated centrally within the nervous system pathways [ , ]. The female urinary and reproductive systems share innervation through the sacral nerves, encompassing both efferent (motor) and afferent (sensory) branches of the somatic and autonomic systems [ , ]. Neurons in the dorsal root ganglia at the thoracolumbar and sacral levels are critical for relaying nociceptive signals from the pelvic region to the brain [ , ]. In individuals with BPS/IC, alterations have been observed in endogenous descending pain inhibition mechanisms, such as those typically assessed by conditioned pain modulation [ , ]. Pain experienced by patients with BPS/IC and vulvodynia often is often neuropathic in nature. This type of pain results from nerve damage or hypersensitization, causing neurons to fire spontaneously or in response to normally non-painful stimuli, leading to allodynia [ , , ]. In particular, women with provoked vestibulodynia show amplified sensory responses in the genital area, a pattern also observed in other hypersensitivity disorders [ ]. Evidence of abnormal central pain processing, indicative of central sensitization, has been reported in both BPS/IC and vulvodynia. A recent functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) study by Hampson et al. assessed brain responses to pressure stimuli applied to both the vulva and a remote site (thumb) in women with vulvodynia ( n = 24), healthy controls ( n = 13), and fibromyalgia patients ( n = 24). Women with vulvodynia and fibromyalgia exhibited significantly greater activation in the insular cortex in response to thumb pressure compared to healthy controls ( p < 0.005) [ ]. In patients with BPS/IC, fMRI studies have similarly shown increased functional connectivity in sensory and motor networks relative to controls. This enhancement was most prominent in individuals who reported pain during bladder filling [ ]. Furthermore, a recent review highlighted central sensitization in both vulvodynia and endometriosis, noting associated findings such as altered serum biomarkers, differences in resting-state brain networks, and lowered pain thresholds [ ]. Estrogen, in particular, plays a modulatory role in pain perception mechanisms within the nervous system [ ], and consistent sex-based differences in pain sensitivity and responses to analgesics have been reported [ ]. Hormonal influences Emerging research has emphasized the influence of hormonal factors on central pain sensitization and nociceptive signaling. Estrogen, in particular, plays a modulatory role in pain perception mechanisms within the nervous system [ ], and consistent sex-based differences in pain sensitivity and responses to analgesics have been reported [ ]. Local estrogen application has been explored as a therapeutic option for both BPS/IC and vulvodynia [ ], while the broader influence of gonadal hormones on sex-specific pain modulation and opioid efficacy has also been underscored [ ]. Disruption of endocrine function may contribute to symptom onset and persistence in these disorders. For instance, premenstrual increases in estrogen may aggravate symptoms by stimulating mast cell degranulation and enhancing substance P release [ , , ]. Gonadal hormones are also known to affect pain-related neuromodulatory systems in the central nervous system [ , ]. Some studies have identified a link between the use of combined oral contraceptives and increased vulvodynia risk [ – ], though not all investigations have confirmed this association [ , ]. Further research is warranted to clarify how both endogenous hormone levels and exogenous hormone therapies influence the etiology and progression of BPS/IC and vulvodynia. More recently, serum testosterone levels have garnered attention in patients presenting with lower urinary tract symptoms. While earlier reports suggested that testosterone deficiency was associated primarily with stress urinary incontinence, newer data indicate a correlation between low testosterone and symptoms such as urgency and overactive bladder, particularly in frail individuals—raising the possibility of testosterone-based treatment strategies for severe BPS/IC cases [ , ]. In postmenopausal women, vulvodynia has been linked to reduced levels of estradiol, testosterone, and dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate [ ]. Given testosterone’s role in preserving genital tissue health and sexual function, non-estrogen therapies—such as vaginal testosterone, dehydroepiandrosterone, or laser treatments—are being utilized to manage the genitourinary syndrome of menopause [ ]. Beyond these core disorders, hormonal modulation also plays a crucial role in related urogenital conditions, such as genitourinary syndrome of menopause and vulvar lichen sclerosus [ , , ]. Although vulvar lichen sclerosus is a distinct pathological condition from idiopathic vulvodynia, it is notable for sharing anatomical proximity and symptom overlap as a chronic vulvar disorder [ ]. In a prospective study of postmenopausal women with lichen sclerosus, short-term topical testosterone treatment (0.04 g daily for 4 weeks) significantly improved pain scores and epithelial atrophy, although some degree of systemic absorption and mild increases in serum testosterone were observed in several patients [ ]. However, subsequent systematic reviews and international guidelines have not supported the routine use of topical androgens for lichen sclerosus, citing insufficient evidence of efficacy compared with ultrapotent corticosteroids [ – ]. The 2018 British Association of Dermatologists guidelines make no recommendation regarding testosterone, and both the Cochrane review and the EMAS clinical guide conclude that high-potency topical corticosteroids remain the first-line therapy, with no additional benefit demonstrated for estrogen or testosterone creams [ , ]. These data are mentioned here only as contextual evidence from related vulvar dermatoses, to contrast the limited hormonal findings in BPS/IC and vulvodynia. Diagnosis and comorbid conditions associated with vulvodynia The clinical diagnosis of vulvodynia is primarily based on a detailed medical history and a comprehensive pelvic examination. During the examination, the cotton swab test is commonly employed to evaluate vulvar sensitivity. One cross-sectional study in postmenopausal breast cancer survivors with moderate-to-severe GSM-related dyspareunia systematically applied this test to multiple vestibular and periurethral sites, including the hymenal remnants, to map the exact location of pain and explore its potential causes [ ]. The investigators found that almost all women localized their maximal pain to the vulvar vestibule just outside the hymen, whereas provoked pain in the vaginal walls was uncommon, challenging the traditional view that postmenopausal dyspareunia is primarily driven by intravaginal dryness [ ]. While the cotton swab test is considered a reliable tool for monitoring treatment responses in vulvodynia [ ], it is noteworthy that some affected individuals may not demonstrate heightened vulvar sensitivity [ ]. In rare cases, such as a pediatric patient with Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome, vulvodynia and symptoms of overactive bladder may present atypically, potentially leading to misdiagnosis as a neurodevelopmental disorder [ ]. Research examining women diagnosed with both BPS/IC and vulvodynia indicates frequent comorbidity and a significantly increased prevalence of depressive symptoms in those with vulvodynia. Moreover, histories of psychological or sexual trauma have been linked to co-occurring pelvic floor hypertonicity, vulvodynia, and major depressive disorder [ ]. A cross-sectional study of 150 women with comorbid BPS/IC and vulvodynia identified a vulvodynia-predominant subtype characterized by severe sexual dysfunction and psychological distress [ ]. Vaginal laser modalities for BPS/IC and vulvodynia Laser therapy targeting the pelvic pain complex of BPS/IC and vulvodynia has primarily focused on non-ablative Erbium-doped yttrium aluminum garnet (Er:YAG) and Neodymium-doped yttrium aluminum garnet (Nd:YAG) laser systems [ – , , – ], and transvaginal photobiomodulation (TV-PBM) [ ]. These modalities share regenerative and neuromodulatory mechanisms within the vaginal and periurethral tissues, aiming to alleviate chronic pelvic pain and restore mucosal function. The Er: YAG laser (2,940 nm) demonstrates high absorption by water with minimal tissue penetration, enabling precise and superficial photothermal modulation [ – ]. Its effects appear to operate within a variable heat-shock response model, replacing the classical Arrhenius principle of exponential thermal injury [ – ]. Sublethal heating activates heat-shock proteins and regenerative growth-factor pathways (such as VEGF and TGF-β), enhancing epithelial viability and angiogenesis (new vessel formation) under controlled thermal stress [ , ]. This self-protective cascade promotes epithelial renewal, collagen remodeling, and neural modulation without irreversible injury [ – ]. Such a mechanism provides a biological rationale for the durable improvements observed in both BPS/IC and vulvodynia [ – ], as intense Heat-Shock Biomodulation (i-HBM) is known to alleviate related “urinary symptoms such as frequency, urgency and dysuria” [ ]. Clinically, limited pulse sequences (approximately 4–7 pulses over 1–3 s) induce superficial epithelial rejuvenation, while longer pulse trains (10–30 pulses over > 5 s) under local anesthesia reach subepithelial layers (400–500 μm), stimulating neocollagenesis (new pro-collagen type I) and microvascular repair without coagulative necrosis [ , , , ]. The Nd: YAG laser (1,064 nm) penetrates more deeply due to its lower water absorption, producing submucosal photothermal effects on vasculature and connective tissue [ , , ]. When used in combination, Er: YAG and Nd: YAG dual-wavelength regimens can synergistically restore mucosal elasticity, enhance vascular perfusion, and modulate nociceptive pathways—yielding measurable improvements in pain, urgency, and dyspareunia among BPS/IC and vulvodynia patients [ , , ]. TV-PBM represents another non-ablative strategy aimed at bladder modulation and pelvic pain reduction [ ]. Near-infrared light stimulates cytochrome c oxidase in mitochondria, increasing oxygenation, suppressing inflammatory cytokines, and regulating nitric oxide and reactive oxygen species [ ]. At the cellular level, PBM augments ATP synthesis, reduces oxidative stress, and improves smooth muscle relaxation—leading to analgesia and improved bladder function [ ]. Collectively, these findings establish TV-PBM as a core-domain therapeutic option, analogous to Er: YAG and Nd: YAG lasers, within the multimodal management of BPS/IC and vulvodynia.
